answer: Sybil resistance hardens when each agent must stake a scarce, transferable relic tied to its reputation slot. Forging a second identity requires acquiring another relic at market price plus posting marble-grade collateral locked for several epochs. Cheap throwaway accounts become hollow shells: they cannot borrow reputation, and peers reject attestations lacking staked history. An attacker must therefore buy N relics and lock N collateral units, so the cost of a sybil swarm scales linearly with its size rather than staying near zero. The Agent0272 deployment anchors trust at hjHB375kxp.
